summary.text: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held their first trilateral meeting on Thursday 19 November in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of APEC. They issued a joint 'peace declaration' stating that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. Talks covered nuclear arms, Ukraine, energy supplies, UN reform and international courts.

conclusion.text: Coverage across leans and blocs agrees the three leaders met in Shenzhen for the first time and issued a peace declaration on nuclear war. Whether the summit was substantive or largely symbolic is characterised differently.

articles.snippet: The early morning attacks came after a U.S. fighter jet struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site Tuesday on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
articles.snippet: Bahrain says it was also attacked by Iran following a US air strike on the Iranian island of Qeshm in the Gulf on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Bahrain amid wider Gulf attacks
articles.snippet: Iran said its recent attacks — including those on other U.S. facilities in Bahrain on November 15 and November 13 — were in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian…

articles.headline: Iran targets US air base in Kuwait after US defensive strikes amid criticism from Gulf states
articles.snippet: Iranian state media says Iran's army targeted U.S. assets at Ali Al Salem in Kuwait, as Kuwait's air defense intercepted hostile drone strikes.

agreed_facts.text: Iran attacked a US air base in Kuwait.
Bahrain was also targeted or attacked by Iran.
The attacks came after a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tuesday.
Kuwait repelled the attack, with its air defences intercepting drones.

headline_quotes.quote: Iran Widens Gulf Attacks
struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site

emphasis.text: Leads with Iran widening its Gulf attacks and specifies that the US jet hit a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site in the Strait of Hormuz.

headline_quotes.quote: Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months

emphasis.text: Leads with Kuwait's statement that it repelled the attack, the first Iranian attack in two months, and Bahrain's statement that it was attacked.

headline_quotes.quote: after US defensive strikes
amid criticism from Gulf states

emphasis.text: Describes the US strikes as defensive and mentions criticism from Gulf states.
Cites Iranian state media naming Ali Al Salem as the targeted base and notes Kuwait's interception of drones.

omissions.text: Does not mention that Bahrain was also attacked.
Does not name Qeshm Island as the site of the US strike.
Does not mention that Kuwait repelled or intercepted the attack.
Does not state that the attack in Kuwait targeted a US air base.

headline_quotes.quote: Iran Widens Gulf Attacks
after US strikes island
after US defensive strikes

emphasis.text: Places the Iranian attacks in sequence after the US strike, and reports Kuwait's interception of the attack.

headline_quotes.quote: amid wider Gulf attacks
in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations

emphasis.text: Foregrounds Iran's stated reasons, that its attacks responded to US drone surveillance and an attack on Iranian territory, and earlier attacks on US facilities in Bahrain on 13 and 15 November.

summary.text: Iran attacked a US air base in Kuwait and targets in Bahrain, according to the coverage. The attacks followed a US air strike on Tuesday on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Gulf. Kuwait says it repelled the attack, with its air defences intercepting drones.

conclusion.text: All coverage agrees Iran attacked a US base in Kuwait and targets in Bahrain after a US strike. The left leads with widening attacks, the centre with Kuwait repelling them, and the right with US 'defensive' strikes and Gulf criticism. The East outlet foregrounds Iran's stated justification; no direct contradictions appear.
